title: Quantisation confound: the base is a 2-bit archive and the tuned model a 4-bit export - two variables changed at once
corrected_statement: The shipped archive is CQ 2-bit and the local exporter can only write 4 bits (needle/model/quantize.py:61 WEIGHT_BITS=4; package METADATA line 99: 'Local fine-tuning trains and exports at 4 bits. The 2-bit post-training ... run on the Cactus Platform'), so every base-vs-tuned difference mixes LoRA with a precision change. Sizes: base needle3.cact 35,335,380 bytes vs tuned.cact 63,474,900 bytes = 1.80x, undisclosed in a paper that sells a 35 MB on-device model. The finished v2 control quantifies it: quantisation alone is worth field F1 +0.069 [+0.033,+0.106] (sys) / +0.057 [+0.020,+0.094] (nosys) with no tool-accuracy change - about a quarter of the total base->tuned gain - and it costs exact-match accuracy (-0.088 [-0.133,-0.042] nosys). The confound is real; the tuning effect survives it. The per-tensor bit census (115 tensors at 2 bits vs 122 at 4 bits) is a reviewer's struct parse I did not repeat.
